thread:
deploy-bot: [deploybot] Starting release window for release/v1.9.3 — feature flag `new-routing-guard` set to CANARY
deploy-bot: cohorts: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Safety pause at each step. Health checks: 200 OK rate, error_rate, p95 latency.
jun: I'm on watch. Plan to pin routing-config to model-v2-canary for first two cohorts. @maria FYI for release notes.
nina: Can we start at 0.2% for EU region? traffic shape spikes there. Prefer snapback policy: if p95 > 350ms or error_rate > 0.8% -> snapback to previous cohort and pause for 15m.
leo: Agree on snapback rule. Also recommend quantized model for 10% to 50% to control cost (pin to model-v2-q).
maria: Release notes checklist: 1) FF name + exact toggle key `new-routing-guard` 2) list pinned versions and how to unpin 3) rollback commands 4) change window UTC 02:00-03:00 5) owner contact @jun
jun: Rollback criteria: if any cohort sees +1% baseline error or sustained traffic drop >10% for 5m -> immediate rollback. Command to rollback: `deployctl ff set new-routing-guard off --reason "auto-snapback"`
deploy-bot: health-monitor: cohort 2% -> p95 420ms, error_rate 1.2% -> ACTION: Pausing ramp. Auto-snapback scheduled.
maria: I'm initiating manual rollback per runbook.
maria: `/deployctl ff set new-routing-guard off --comment "paused: p95>350ms"`
deploy-bot: Toggle applied. new-routing-guard = OFF. Notifying oncall.
jun: Thanks. I'll leave the pin in place for another hour to drain sessions then unpin. Logging this incident for postmortem.
nina: Adding note to release notes draft: "Paused at 2% due to latency regression in EU; rolled back; follow-up: perf tuning for cache warmup."
leo: After we unstick, let's rerun a narrower canary next week with longer soak at 0.2% and KV cache priming.
maria: Agreed. I'll mark change window as aborted and update release notes and ship a short email to stakeholders.
jun: Closing thread — will attach metrics snapshot and timing.
